messages.subject: Question about the linear models
parts:
Hello geomorph community,

I am trying to access differences in shape between 2 lineages of a single species. I am not necessarily interested in sexual dimorphism. I have an unbalanced data (different numbers of specimens for each lineage) so I am using SS.type = "II". 

My HOS  test: 

fit_unique_mb <- procD.lm(coords~log(Csize), 
                          data = data_mb,
                          iter = 999,
                          print.progress = TRUE)

fit_common_mb <- procD.lm(coords~log(Csize) + Lineage,
                          data = data_mb,
                          iter = 999,
                          print.progress = TRUE,
                          SS.type = "II")
anova(fit_common_mb, fit_unique_mb, print.progress = TRUE)

gives me a non-singnificant interaction. Which led me to conclude that I have a common allometry effect. I am attatching a plot to this.

My question is: do I necessarily need to include sex as a factor (something like Lineage*Sex) to make post-hoc inferences with the pairwise function? Since I am only interested in shape differences between lineages. Or is that not necessary?

--
Diniz Ferreira
Graduando em Ciências Biológicas
Laboratório de Evolução e Genética de Insetos (LEGIN)
DEZG - IB - Universidade Federal de Pelotas

messages.author: 4d71c6e24fb21497
messages.subject: RE: [geomorph-r-package] Question about the linear models
parts:
Diniz,

 

You did not test the interaction because it was not included in the model. You have:

 

coords~log(Csize) + Lineage,

 

You need: coords~log(Csize) * Lineage,

 

And then evaluate the interaction term.

 

Dean
